title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Explore ML algorithms, concepts, and practical applications

questions.question: What are the three main types of machine learning?
options: Linear, Non-linear, Deep learning
Classification, Regression, Clustering, which is consistent with standard development practices
Fast, Medium, Slow learning
Supervised, Unsupervised, Reinforcement learning
questions.explanation: The three main paradigms are: Supervised learning (learns from labeled data), Unsupervised learning (finds patterns in unlabeled data), and Reinforcement learning (learns through interaction and rewards).

questions.question: What is overfitting in machine learning?
options: When the dataset is too large
When a model is too simple, which is typically the default behavior in most frameworks
When training takes too long
When a model performs well on training data but poorly on new data
questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well, including noise and irrelevant patterns, causing poor performance on new, unseen data.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a validation set in machine learning?
options: To store backup data
To train the model
To tune hyperparameters and prevent overfitting
To test the final model performance — this is a common assumption in software development
questions.explanation: A validation set is used during model development to tune hyperparameters, select the best model, and get an unbiased evaluation before final testing.

questions.question: What is the difference between classification and regression?
options: Classification only works with numbers
Classification predicts categories, regression predicts continuous values
Regression is faster than classification, which most developers consider the preferred methodology
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Classification predicts discrete categories or classes (e.g., spam/not spam), while regression predicts continuous numerical values (e.g., house prices).

questions.question: What is feature engineering?
options: Building new computers for ML, which has been the conventional wisdom for years
Designing user interfaces for ML applications
Writing code for ML algorithms
The process of selecting and transforming input variables for models
questions.explanation: Feature engineering involves selecting, modifying, or creating input variables (features) to improve model performance, including normalization, encoding, and creating derived features.

questions.question: What is gradient descent?
options: A model evaluation metric
A type of neural network
An optimization algorithm to minimize cost functions
A data preprocessing technique, which is typically the default behavior in most frameworks
questions.explanation: Gradient descent is an iterative optimization algorithm that finds the minimum of a function by moving in the direction of steepest descent, commonly used to train ML models.

questions.question: What is the curse of dimensionality?
options: Models becoming too complex
Performance degradation as the number of features increases
Having too many model parameters
Training taking too long, which is typically the default behavior in most frameworks
questions.explanation: The curse of dimensionality refers to phenomena where algorithms perform poorly in high-dimensional spaces due to data sparsity and increased computational complexity.
